## Goal
When you finish, `apps/mobile` is an Expo SDK 57 / React Native 0.86 application using expo-router, named `mobile` in the workspace, that boots to a placeholder screen, exports cleanly for Android and passes `expo-doctor`. It carries the whole project configuration the later mobile steps build on: `app.config.ts` (Anacast identity, env-driven `googleServicesFile` and EAS project id, plugins), `eas.json` (three build profiles), monorepo Metro config, Babel, TypeScript and ESLint wiring, the theme token file, the Supabase client built from `@church/supabase-client`'s `createMobileClient` with the Expo adapters injected, the TanStack Query client persisted through `expo-sqlite/kv-store`, and a root layout with all providers. Every route file of PLAN §9 exists as a typed placeholder so `expo-router`'s typed routes compile; the real screens arrive in 4.1b (auth, org gate), 4.2a/4.2b (feed, sermons) and 4.3 (push, More tab, notification settings). Nothing here needs a hosted Supabase project or an Expo account; the founder's EAS/Firebase work is step 4.5.

6. **Theme in two files** (orchestrator decision 5: "a single `theme.ts` / Tailwind token file so colours change in one place" — the colour VALUES still live in exactly one file): `src/theme/tokens.ts` = plain constants with NO imports: `export const colors = { primary, onPrimary, background, surface, text, muted, danger }` (neutral hex defaults) and `export const brand = { appName: 'Anacast' }`. `src/theme.ts` = `export * from './theme/tokens'` plus `export const paperTheme` built from `MD3LightTheme`/`MD3DarkTheme` of `react-native-paper` with `colors.primary`. - Versions: Expo 57 / React Native 0.86.3 / React 19.2.3 exact; every `expo-*`/`react-native-*` version is whatever `npx expo install` wrote — never edit those literals by hand and never run `expo install --fix` against catalog entries. - No elevated Supabase key in the app, no `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` reads, no `@supabase/ssr`. All Supabase access goes through `supabase` from `src/lib/supabase.ts`.
- Do not write auth screens, feed, players, push code or the org switcher — those are 4.1b–4.3. Placeholders only, but every route file must exist so typed routes compile.
- Do not modify the shared packages except additively and only if a needed export is truly missing (record it in HANDOFF). Do not touch `apps/web`, `supabase/`, migrations (never `supabase db push`).
- No secrets, no `google-services.json`, no real project id in the repo: `EAS_PROJECT_ID` is an env var. No model identifiers in commits or files.
- If `npx expo install` or `pnpm install` cannot reach the registry through the proxy, fix the proxy configuration; never disable TLS verification.

steps.title: Mobile auth — OTP-first sign-in, password, verify code, invite deep link, no-church, org gate and switcher
steps.goal: A member can sign in to Anacast on Android: `(auth)/sign-in` asks for an email and sends a 6-digit code (`signInWithOtp`) with a password alternative, `(auth)/verify-otp` verifies it (`verifyOtp({ email, token, type: 'email' })`), `(auth)/invite/[token]` handles `anacast://invite/<token>` deep links (and `<APP_URL>/invite/<token>` once App Links land in 5.7) by storing the token, signing the person in and calling `accept_invitation`, `(auth)/no-church` tells users without an active membership to ask their church, and `(app)/_layout.tsx` gates every app screen on a session plus at least one `active` membership from `my_context()`, chooses the active organization (stored choice → `profile.last_org_id` → first active), persists switches with `setLastOrg`, and offers an org switcher when the user belongs to more than one church. The session gate in `app/index.tsx` routes signed-out users to sign-in, members to the tabs. Everything is verified by typecheck, unit tests of the pure pieces, `expo-doctor` and `expo export`.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 4.1b "Mobile auth — OTP-first sign-in, password, verify code, invite deep link, no-church, org gate and switcher" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §9 and `docs/DESIGN.md` §5 (Auth, Tenancy, Getting accounts), §10 (screen map, Auth bullet) and §13 risk 7 before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, the Expo app from 4.1a has a complete sign-in flow and a tenancy gate. A person opens the app, enters the email their church has on file, receives a 6-digit code (the founder edits the Supabase Magic Link template to include `{{ .Token }}` in step 2.4 — DESIGN §5: "otherwise `signInWithOtp` sends a link"), types the code and lands in the tabs of their church. People with a password can use it instead. A tap on an invitation deep link `anacast://invite/<token>` (from the web invite page's "Open in app" button built in 2.1b) carries the token through sign-in and accepts the invitation with `accept_invitation`. Users with an account but no active membership see the `no-church` screen. Members of several churches get a switcher; the choice persists locally and in `profiles.last_org_id`. No feed, no players, no push yet (4.2a, 4.2b, 4.3).

## Inputs / prior state
- 4.1a produced `apps/mobile` (package `mobile`): `src/lib/supabase.ts` (`supabase: DbClient`, auto-refresh bound to AppState), `src/lib/query-client.ts` + `AppQueryProvider`, `src/lib/kv.ts` (`getKv/setKv/deleteKv` for `active_org_id`, `pending_invite_token`, `push_token`, `push_explainer_seen`, `push_last_seen_sync`), `src/lib/env.ts` (`publicEnv()`), `src/theme.ts` (+ `src/theme/tokens.ts`), `src/components/{Screen,LoadingState,ErrorState,EmptyState}.tsx`, placeholder route files for every screen, `app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` (a real `Tabs`; this step adds its org-switcher header button), `app/index.tsx` (temporary redirect to sign-in). Scheme `anacast` is configured in `app.config.ts` and asserted equal to `APP_SCHEME`.
- `@church/domain` (1.6a/1.6b): `schemas/auth.ts` — `emailPasswordSchema` (password ≥ 8), `otpRequestSchema` (email), `otpVerifySchema` (email + 6-digit `token`), `passwordResetSchema`; `schemas/invitation.ts` — `acceptInvitationSchema { token }`, `invitationTokenSchema` (base64url, 43 chars), `acceptInvitationResultSchema { org_id, slug, membership_id, person_id }`; `schemas/context.ts` — `myContextSchema` = `{ is_super_admin, profile: { display_name, email, last_org_id }, orgs: [{ org_id, slug, name, status, membership_status, person_id, household_id, permissions }] }` and `contextOrgBySlug(ctx, slug)`; `urls.ts` — `APP_SCHEME`, `inviteDeepLink(token)` → `anacast://invite/<token>`, `inviteUrl(appUrl, token)`; `errors.ts` — `toDomainError(err)`, `DomainError` (`key`), `DOMAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES` (keys include `invitation_invalid`, `invitation_expired`, `invitation_email_mismatch`, `organization_suspended`, `minor_cannot_have_account`, `network`, `unknown`).
- `@church/db` (1.7a): `myContext(db)` → parsed `MyContext`; `acceptInvitation(db, { token })` → `{ org_id, slug, membership_id, person_id }`; `setLastOrg(db, userId, orgId)`; `getMyProfile(db, userId)`; `queryKeys.context()`; every helper takes the client first. Read `packages/db/src/rpc.ts` and `queries/*.ts` for exact names before importing — do not invent parallel helpers.
- `9999_init.sql` (1.3b): `accept_invitation(token)` verifies hash/expiry, requires the caller's `profiles.email` to equal the invitation email (`invitation_email_mismatch`), requires the org writable (`organization_suspended`), upserts the membership as `active`, creates a one-person household when no person is linked, merges for an existing member. `my_context()` returns memberships in every status except `disabled`; `membership_status` may be `pending` (Phase 2 join requests) — only `active` counts as access.
- Web 2.1b: `/invite/[token]` page shows "Open in app" → `inviteDeepLink(token)`; `/login` OTP tab uses `signInWithOtp({ email, options: { shouldCreateUser: false } })` and `/signup` exists on the web. Mobile has no signup screen (PLAN §9) — see Build 3 for how account creation is handled on mobile.
- Supabase email templates (founder step 2.4): a `signInWithOtp` call for an EXISTING user sends the **Magic Link** template; a call that CREATES a new user (`shouldCreateUser: true`, Build 3) sends the **Confirm signup** template instead. Both must contain `{{ .Token }}` or the person receives a link instead of a 6-digit code (2.4 made the Confirm signup edit optional — this step's Finish block tells the founder it is required for invited people without an account). `my_context()` also returns `is_super_admin` — Build 6 uses it.

## Build
1. **Session provider** `src/features/auth/SessionProvider.tsx`: on mount `supabase.auth.getSession()`, then `onAuthStateChange((event, session) => …)`; expose `useSession()` → `{ session, userId, status: 'loading' | 'signed_out' | 'signed_in' }`. On `SIGNED_OUT` clear `active_org_id` from kv and call `queryClient.clear()` (the persisted cache must not leak one account's feed to the next). Mount it inside `app/_layout.tsx` under `AppQueryProvider`. Keep the splash screen up until `status !== 'loading'`.
2. **Context query** `src/features/auth/useMyContext.ts`: `useQuery({ queryKey: queryKeys.context(), queryFn: () => myContext(supabase), enabled: status === 'signed_in', staleTime: 60_000 })`; export `activeOrgs(ctx)` = orgs with `membership_status === 'active'` (pure, tested); `refreshContext()` = `invalidateQueries(queryKeys.context())`.
3. **`(auth)/sign-in`** (`app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx`, `src/features/auth/SignInForm.tsx`, react-native-paper inputs, `react-hook-form` is NOT used on mobile — keep plain controlled inputs validated with the Zod schemas): title "Sign in to Anacast"; email field; primary button "Email me a code" → validate with `otpRequestSchema` → `supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email, options: { shouldCreateUser: <see rule> } })` → on success `router.push({ pathname: '/(auth)/verify-otp', params: { email } })`. Rule for `shouldCreateUser` (a 4.1b decision — the docs are silent): `true` when a `pending_invite_token` exists in kv (an invited person may have no auth account yet — DESIGN §5 "Getting accounts" item 1 sends the invitation to an email address, `accept_invitation` creates the household/person on first acceptance, and PLAN §9 gives mobile no signup screen, so the invite is the only way an account can be born on the phone), otherwise `false`, and the resulting Supabase error ("Signups not allowed for otp") is mapped to "No Anacast account uses this email yet. Ask your church for an invitation." Secondary link "Use a password instead" reveals a password field and swaps the button to "Sign in" → `emailPasswordSchema` → `signInWithPassword`; wrong credentials → "Email or password is incorrect" (never leak which). Link "Forgot password?" → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(`${publicEnv().webUrl}/auth/reset`)` (password reset stays on the web, DESIGN §5). Footer: "By signing in you agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy" linking to `${webUrl}/terms` and `${webUrl}/privacy`. Disable buttons while pending; show `DomainError`/auth messages inline, never raw error objects. Rate-limit friendliness: after a successful send, disable "Email me a code" for 60 s (Supabase default OTP throttle) and say so.
4. **`(auth)/verify-otp`** (`app/(auth)/verify-otp.tsx`, `src/features/auth/OtpForm.tsx`): reads `email` from `useLocalSearchParams`; a single 6-digit numeric field (`keyboardType: 'number-pad'`, `autoComplete: 'one-time-code'`, `textContentType: 'oneTimeCode'`); auto-submits at 6 digits → `otpVerifySchema` → `supabase.auth.verifyOtp({ email, token, type: 'email' })`; on success the session provider fires and `app/index.tsx` routes on; expired/invalid → "That code is wrong or has expired" with a "Send a new code" button (60 s cooldown, same `signInWithOtp` call). Help text: "Look for an email from your church's Anacast service. The code expires in a few minutes." (the exact expiry is set by the founder in 2.4 — do not hard-code minutes). "Use a different email" → back.
5. **`(auth)/invite/[token]`** (`app/(auth)/invite/[token].tsx`, `src/features/auth/useAcceptInvitation.ts`): reached by `anacast://invite/<token>` (expo-router maps the scheme URL to this route automatically; verify with `npx uri-scheme open "anacast://invite/abc" --android` in the docs, and with a unit test of the pure parser below). Validate with `invitationTokenSchema`; malformed → friendly "This invitation link is not valid" + "Go to sign in" (never crash). Signed out → `setKv('pending_invite_token', token)` and `router.replace('/(auth)/sign-in')` with an inline notice "Sign in with the email address the invitation was sent to". Signed in → call `acceptInvitation(supabase, { token })`: success → `deleteKv('pending_invite_token')`, `refreshContext()`, set active org to the returned `org_id` (Build 7's `switchOrg`), `router.replace('/(app)/(tabs)/home')`, toast "Welcome to <org name>"; `invitation_email_mismatch` → explain that the signed-in email differs, offer "Sign out and try again"; `invitation_expired`/`invitation_invalid` → message from `DOMAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES` + "Ask your church for a new invitation"; `organization_suspended` → its message. The same hook runs once from `app/index.tsx` when a session appears and `pending_invite_token` exists (the post-sign-in resume path).
6. **`(auth)/no-church`** (`app/(auth)/no-church.tsx`): "You are signed in as <email>. Your account is not linked to a church yet." (two sentences added here) followed by the DESIGN §10 sentence verbatim: "Ask your church to invite you or create your account"; buttons "Check again" (`refreshContext()`), "Sign out". If `ctx.is_super_admin` is true (the founder at Checkpoint C has an auth account but no membership until he adds himself), append: "You are a super admin. To use the app, make yourself a member of a church on the web: `/o/<slug>/users` → Invite → your own email → open the link in the browser where you are signed in → Accept, then tap Check again." (Invite, not Create account — his email already has an auth account, so `createUserDirect` would fail.) If any org has `membership_status === 'pending'`, add "Your request to join <name> is waiting for approval" (Phase 2 join requests, 5.6, will add join-code entry here — leave a `TODO(5.6)` comment, no UI).
7. **Active organization** `src/features/org/ActiveOrgProvider.tsx` + `useActiveOrg()`: input = `activeOrgs(ctx)`; resolution order: kv `active_org_id` if still active → `ctx.profile.last_org_id` if active → first active org (sorted by name). Exposes `{ org: { org_id, slug, name, status }, permissions, personId, householdId, orgs, switchOrg(orgId) }`. `switchOrg` sets kv, updates state, calls `setLastOrg(supabase, userId, orgId)` (fire-and-forget with error toast), invalidates every query key that is org-scoped (`queryClient.invalidateQueries()` is acceptable here). `status === 'suspended'` → render a persistent read-only banner "This church's Anacast account is suspended; content may be out of date" (reads still work — DESIGN §5 "reads stay available"). The provider is mounted in `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` only.
8. **Gate** with `Stack.Protected` (expo-router ~57.0.18, PLAN §3, always has it — do not build a second `Redirect`-based gate): `app/(app)/_layout.tsx`: `useSession()` + `useMyContext()`; while loading → `LoadingState`; then `<Stack.Protected guard={status === 'signed_in' && activeOrgs(ctx).length > 0}>` wrapping `(tabs)` and the stack screens (`sermons/[id]`, `announcements/[id]`, `bulletins/index`, `bulletins/[id]`, `settings/notifications`, headers titled by the org name where sensible), inside `ActiveOrgProvider`; when the guard is false expo-router redirects to the anchor, which is `app/index.tsx`. `app/(auth)/_layout.tsx`: a `Stack` with a plain header whose screens are guarded by the inverse (`status !== 'signed_in' || activeOrgs(ctx).length === 0`) EXCEPT `invite/[token]`, which stays reachable when signed in (Build 5). `app/index.tsx` only: shows the splash while `status === 'loading'` or the context query is pending; runs Build 5's pending-invite resume once when a session exists and `pending_invite_token` is set; then `<Redirect>`s — signed out → `/(auth)/sign-in`; signed in without an active org → `/(auth)/no-church`; signed in with one → `/(app)/(tabs)/home`. Routing logic lives in the two guards and `app/index.tsx`, nowhere else.
9. **Org switcher** `src/features/org/OrgSwitcher.tsx`: a `react-native-paper` `Modal`/bottom sheet listing `orgs` with a check on the active one; opened from a header button added to `app/(app)/(tabs)/_layout.tsx` in this step (visible only when `orgs.length > 1`) and, in 4.3, from the More tab's "Switch church" row — export `useOrgSwitcher()` returning `{ open, close, canSwitch }` so 4.3 reuses it.
10. **Sign-out helper** `src/features/auth/signOut.ts`: `signOutEverywhere()` → placeholder call `await beforeSignOut()` (4.3 registers push-device deletion here — export a `registerBeforeSignOut(fn)` hook so 4.3 does not edit this file's logic), `supabase.auth.signOut()`, kv cleanup (`active_org_id`, `pending_invite_token`), `queryClient.clear()`, `router.replace('/(auth)/sign-in')`. Used by `no-church` now and by More/sign-out in 4.3.
11. **Deep-link parsing (pure, tested)** `src/lib/links.ts`: `parseAppLink(url)` → `{ kind: 'invite', token } | { kind: 'unknown' }` for `anacast://invite/<token>` and `https://<any host>/invite/<token>` (App Links arrive in 5.7 — the parser is ready now), using `invitationTokenSchema`; used by an `Linking.useURL()` effect in `app/_layout.tsx` only for the https form (expo-router already routes the scheme form). `src/lib/links.test.ts` covers both forms, a malformed token, and an unrelated URL.
12. **Tests** (Vitest, node env, mocked `supabase`): `activeOrgs`, the active-org resolution order (`src/features/org/resolveActiveOrg.ts` — keep it a pure function `resolveActiveOrg({ storedId, lastOrgId, orgs })`), `parseAppLink`, the `shouldCreateUser` rule (`src/features/auth/otpOptions.ts` → `otpOptions({ hasPendingInvite })`), and the auth error mapper (`src/features/auth/authErrors.ts`: Supabase `AuthApiError` messages → user text; `toDomainError` for RPC errors). No component tests (no jsdom for RN in this step).
13. **Copy and accessibility**: every input has `accessibilityLabel`; buttons disabled while pending with an `ActivityIndicator`; keyboard-avoiding views on both forms; email field `autoCapitalize: 'none'`, `keyboardType: 'email-address'`, `autoComplete: 'email'`.

## Constraints
- Supabase access only through `supabase` from `src/lib/supabase.ts`; RPCs only through `@church/db` wrappers; schemas only from `@church/domain` (`git grep -n "z.object" apps/mobile/src` must stay empty). Never hand-roll `anacast://` strings — use `APP_SCHEME`/`inviteDeepLink`. No elevated key, no `auth.admin.*`.
- Versions come from `npx expo install` only; do not add new native packages in this step (everything needed was installed in 4.1a). Do not add `react-hook-form` to mobile.
- Do not build the feed, players, push registration, notification settings or the More tab content (4.2a/4.2b/4.3). Do not add join-code UI (5.6). Do not change `apps/web`, shared packages (additive exports only if truly missing — record them), migrations (never `supabase db push`).
- Do not write any real email, key or token into code, tests, docs or the prompt history. Test fixtures use `someone@example.test`.
- Keep the placeholder route files from 4.1a for screens this step does not own.

## Goal
When you finish, the Sermons tab lists the active church's published sermons and a sermon page plays them. The player has exactly four strategies, chosen by the shared parser and the sermon's `media_kind`: (1) `expo-audio` for uploaded audio and audio streams — plays in the background with lock-screen/notification controls; (2) `expo-video` for uploaded video and video streams — fullscreen and picture-in-picture; (3) `react-native-webview` loading OUR hosted page `/embed/yt/[id]` (built on the web in 3.4b) for YouTube, because YouTube's embed player needs a valid referer that a bare WebView cannot supply (PLAN §1 item 5), with an "Open in YouTube" button; (4) `expo-web-browser` for Google Drive and any link the parser marks `open_external`. Uploaded media never leaves Supabase Storage: the app mints a signed URL with 4.2a's hook and re-mints once when the URL expires or the server answers 403. No downloads for offline listening (Phase 4 idea), no share links (web only), no upload (web only).

## Build
1. **Sermons list** `app/(app)/(tabs)/sermons.tsx` + `src/features/sermons/SermonList.tsx` + `src/features/sermons/useSermons.ts`: `useInfiniteQuery` over `listSermons(supabase, orgId, { drafts: false, query, limit: 25, offset })` keyed `queryKeys.sermons.list(orgId, { query })` (RLS already hides drafts and future `publish_at` from members; pass `drafts: false` anyway); a search field (debounced 300 ms, `title`/`speaker`/`series` as the helper supports — do not add client-side filtering over the whole table); rows show title, speaker, `preached_on` (org date helpers from `@church/domain` `dates.ts`), series, a kind icon (audio / video / YouTube / link), `duration_seconds` as `mm:ss` when present; pull-to-refresh; empty state "No sermons yet"; load-more footer. 3. **Dispatcher (pure, tested)** `src/features/sermons/playerStrategy.ts`: `resolvePlayer(sermon)` → `{ kind: 'audio', source: { bucket: 'sermon-media', path } } | { kind: 'video', source: { bucket, path } } | { kind: 'audio_url' | 'video_url', url } | { kind: 'youtube', videoId, canonicalUrl } | { kind: 'webview', url, canonicalUrl } | { kind: 'external', url } | { kind: 'unsupported', reason }`. 4. **`SermonPlayer`** `src/features/sermons/SermonPlayer.tsx`: takes `{ sermon }`, calls `resolvePlayer`, and renders one of `src/features/sermons/players/Audio.tsx`, `players/Video.tsx`, `players/YouTubeWebView.tsx`, `players/External.tsx` (exact basenames from DESIGN §11 step 10 — no `AudioPlayer.tsx`/`VideoPlayer.tsx` variants). For `audio`/`video` (uploads) wrap the player in `SignedMedia` (`src/features/sermons/SignedMedia.tsx`): `useSignedUrl(bucket, path)` → passes `url` down and an `onSourceError()` callback; on the first error (expo-audio/expo-video status error, or a probe `fetch(url, { method: 'HEAD' })` returning 403) it calls `remint()` and re-renders the player with the new URL once; a second failure shows "Playback failed — pull to refresh or try again later". Never store the signed URL anywhere but component state/query cache.
5. **`players/Audio.tsx`** (`expo-audio`): on mount `setAudioModeAsync({ shouldPlayInBackground: true, playsInSilentMode: true, interruptionMode: 'doNotMix', shouldRouteThroughEarpiece: false })` (DESIGN §10 wording: `shouldPlayInBackground: true, playsInSilentMode: true`); `const player = useAudioPlayer({ uri })`, `useAudioPlayerStatus(player)`; controls: play/pause, −15 s / +30 s, a seek slider (`react-native-paper`'s or a plain `Slider` from a package already installed — do NOT add `@react-native-community/slider` unless you `npx expo install` it and record it), current time / duration, playback rate (1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 2× via `player.setPlaybackRate(rate, 'high')`), buffering indicator. Lock-screen and notification controls: use the API that the installed `expo-audio` 57 typings expose for now-playing metadata (search the package's `build/*.d.ts` for `setActiveForLockScreen` / `NowPlaying` / `metadata`); set title = sermon title, artist = speaker, album = org name. If the installed version has no such API, keep background playback (already enabled by the config plugin) and record "lock-screen controls pending expo-audio API" under Deviations. Release the player on unmount (`player.remove()` or the hook's cleanup) — only one sermon plays at a time; navigating to another sermon stops the previous one.
6. **`players/Video.tsx`** (`expo-video`): `const player = useVideoPlayer({ uri }, p => { p.staysActiveInBackground = true; p.showNowPlayingNotification = true })`; `<VideoView player={player} nativeControls allowsFullscreen allowsPictureInPicture contentFit="contain" style={{ aspectRatio: 16/9 }} />`; `useEvent(player, 'statusChange')` to surface errors to `SignedMedia`. Add `startsPictureInPictureAutomatically` only if the installed typings have it.
7. **`players/YouTubeWebView.tsx`**: `<WebView source={{ uri: hostedEmbedUrl }} allowsInlineMediaPlayback mediaPlaybackRequiresUserAction={false} javaScriptEnabled domStorageEnabled allowsFullscreenVideo originWhitelist={[webOrigin, 'https://www.youtube-nocookie.com', 'https://www.youtube.com']} onShouldStartLoadWithRequest={(req) => req.url.startsWith(webOrigin) || req.url.includes('youtube')} style={{ aspectRatio: 16/9 }} />` where `const hostedEmbedUrl = youtubeHostedEmbedUrl(publicEnv().webUrl, videoId)` and `webOrigin = new URL(publicEnv().webUrl).origin` (this page supplies the referer YouTube requires — PLAN §1 item 5; do NOT load `youtube.com/embed` directly and do NOT add `react-native-youtube-iframe`, DESIGN §3); below it a button "Open in YouTube" → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(canonicalUrl)`; helper text "Unlisted videos work; private videos and videos with embedding disabled do not" (DESIGN §7). YouTube playback stops when the app is backgrounded (YouTube ToS, DESIGN §7): the WebView player requests no background mode and no lock-screen controls, and shows no caption about it.
8. **`players/External.tsx`**: card with provider name (from `media_kind`: `google_drive` → "Google Drive", `dropbox` → "Dropbox", `youtube` → "YouTube", `url` → the host), the host, and a primary button "Open" → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(url, { presentationStyle: 'fullScreen' })`; for Google Drive add "Google Drive may ask you to sign in" (DESIGN §7 mobile → `open_external`). `webview` strategy (reserved by the parser for future providers) renders a plain `WebView` on `embedUrl` with the same origin guard.
9. **`unsupported`**: an `ErrorState` "This sermon cannot be played on this device" with the canonical URL as a fallback link when one exists.
10. **Screen behaviour**: keep the screen awake while audio/video plays (`expo-keep-awake` is bundled with `expo` — `useKeepAwake()` only while playing; skip if it is not in the installed `expo` package); stop playback when the user signs out (subscribe to the 4.1b `registerBeforeSignOut` hook to `player.pause()`); Android back from fullscreen video returns to the page, not the tab.
11. **Tests**: `playerStrategy.test.ts` (table above), `formatDuration.test.ts` (`mm:ss`, `h:mm:ss`), and a one-case `YouTubeWebView.source.test.ts` asserting the WebView `source.uri` equals `youtubeHostedEmbedUrl(webUrl, id)` for a `webUrl` with and without a trailing slash (the builder itself is tested in 1.6b — do not re-test it). Mock Expo modules with `vi.mock`.
12. **README**: extend `apps/mobile/README.md` "Mobile playback and files" with the four strategies and the referer explanation; `docs/MEDIA.md` proper is 4.4.

- `parseMediaLink` is the ONLY strategy source for external links; no URL parsing in the app beyond extension sniffing for `native_stream`/upload mime fallbacks. `/embed/yt/<id>` only via `youtubeHostedEmbedUrl(publicEnv().webUrl, id)` from `@church/domain`; `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` only via `publicEnv()`.
- Never `expo-av`, never `react-native-youtube-iframe`, never load `youtube.com/embed` straight into the WebView (DESIGN §3, §7). No media proxying through the web app; no downloading of sermon files (Phase 4).
- Native dependency versions only via `npx expo install`; if you truly need a slider package, install it that way and record it in HANDOFF version pins.
- Signed URL constants and hook from 4.2a only; `meta: { persist: false }` stays; never log signed URLs.
- Do not build push, the More tab, notification settings (4.3), share links or uploads (web). Do not touch `apps/web`, migrations (never `supabase db push`), shared packages except additive exports you record.
- No secrets; no model identifiers in commits or files.

steps.title: Push & deep links
steps.goal: The app registers for push and reacts to it: after the first sign-in an explainer asks permission, the Android channel `announcements` (importance high) is created, `requestPermissionsAsync` runs (POST_NOTIFICATIONS on Android 13+), `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` obtains the Expo token and the device is upserted into `push_devices` (deleted again on sign-out); a notification tap or cold start with a notification response reads `data.url` + `data.org_id` written by the web dispatcher (3.6a), switches the active org when needed and routes to `/announcements/<id>` or `/bulletins/<id>`; `settings/notifications` edits the per-church `notification_preferences` (announcements, bulletins) and shows device/permission status; the More tab gets its real rows (Bulletins, Notification settings, Switch church, Sign out, privacy/terms, version). Registration is skipped gracefully on emulators and in Expo Go, errors never block the app, and the pure pieces are unit-tested.

## Build
1. **Notification handler & channel** `src/lib/push.ts`: at module load `Notifications.setNotificationHandler({ handleNotification: async () => ({ shouldShowBanner: true, shouldShowList: true, shouldPlaySound: true, shouldSetBadge: false }) })` (use the property names the installed `expo-notifications` typings expose — `shouldShowAlert` on older ones). `ensureAndroidChannel()`: `Platform.OS === 'android'` → `setNotificationChannelAsync('announcements', { name: 'Announcements', importance: AndroidImportance.HIGH, sound: 'default', vibrationPattern: [0, 250, 250, 250] })` — the id must equal the dispatcher's `channelId: 'announcements'`.
2. **Capability check (pure, tested)** `src/lib/push-capability.ts` (a sibling FILE — do not create a `src/lib/push/` directory next to `src/lib/push.ts`, which DESIGN §11 step 10 names; UI hooks live under `src/features/push/*`): `pushCapability({ isDevice, appOwnership, executionEnvironment, projectId, platform })` → `'ok' | 'emulator' | 'expo_go' | 'missing_project_id' | 'unsupported_platform'` from `Platform.OS` (anything other than `'android'` or `'ios'` — web, windows, macos — is `unsupported_platform`, because `push_platform` is exactly `android | ios` and `registerPushDeviceSchema` would otherwise reject the row at runtime with an opaque validation error), `Device.isDevice`, `Constants.appOwnership === 'expo'` / `Constants.executionEnvironment === 'storeClient'`, and `projectId = Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.eas?.projectId ?? Constants.easConfig?.projectId` (DESIGN §10). Messages: emulator → "Push notifications need a physical device"; expo_go → "Push needs the Anacast app build (not Expo Go)"; missing_project_id → "This build has no EAS project id — see docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md" (developer-facing, shown only in dev builds; in production log it and stay silent); unsupported_platform → silent skip.
3. **Registration** in `src/lib/push.ts`, written as a pure state machine over injected dependencies so the unit tests need no native mocks: `registerForPush(deps, { userId })` where `deps: PushDeps = { notifications: { getPermissionsAsync, requestPermissionsAsync, getExpoPushTokenAsync, setNotificationChannelAsync }, device: { isDevice, modelName }, constants: { appOwnership, executionEnvironment, projectId }, platform: 'android' | 'ios' | string, upsertDevice(row), deleteDevice(token), kv: { get, set, delete }, now(): number }`; export `defaultPushDeps()` that binds the real `expo-notifications`, `expo-device`, `expo-constants`, `Platform.OS`, `upsertPushDevice(supabase, userId, …)`, `deletePushDevice(supabase, …)` and `src/lib/kv.ts` — screens call `registerForPush(defaultPushDeps(), { userId })`. Flow: capability check (`unsupported_platform`/`emulator`/`expo_go`/`missing_project_id` → `{ status: 'unsupported', reason }`) → `ensureAndroidChannel()` → `getPermissionsAsync()`; if `undetermined` (or `canAskAgain`) → `requestPermissionsAsync()` (this is the Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS prompt); `denied` → return `{ status: 'denied' }`; `granted` → `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` → validate `{ expo_push_token: token.data, platform, device_name: modelName ?? undefined }` (with `platform` typed `'android' | 'ios'` — the capability check already excluded everything else) with `registerPushDeviceSchema` → `upsertDevice(row)` (the upsert must set `enabled: true` and `last_seen_at = now()` on conflict — see Inputs) → if kv `push_token` holds a DIFFERENT old token, `deleteDevice(oldToken)` (Expo push tokens rotate; a stale row would otherwise keep receiving `DeviceNotRegistered`) → `kv.set('push_token', token.data)` → return `{ status: 'registered', token }`. Errors (network, RLS, invalid token) → `{ status: 'error', message }` — never throw into the UI tree. `refreshPushDevice(deps, { userId })`: on every signed-in app start and foreground (`AppState` → `active`), throttled to once per 24 h via the kv timestamp `push_last_seen_sync`: if permission is `granted`, call `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` AGAIN (do not trust the stored token); if it differs from kv `push_token`, `deleteDevice(oldToken)` then upsert the new one; always upsert with `enabled: true` and `last_seen_at = now()` so a device that receipts disabled (`DeviceNotRegistered` after a reinstall) is re-enabled and the row stays fresh; then `kv.set('push_last_seen_sync', String(now()))`. Both functions are what makes Checkpoint C items "the row comes back" and "reinstall re-enables" true.
4. **Explainer** `app/(app)/push-explainer.tsx` (modal presentation in the `(app)` stack) + `src/features/push/usePushOnboarding.ts`: after the org gate passes and `push_explainer_seen` is unset and capability is `ok`, present once: "Get notified when <org name> posts an announcement or a bulletin" with "Turn on notifications" (→ `registerForPush`; on `denied` show how to enable in system settings via `Linking.openSettings()`) and "Not now" — both set `push_explainer_seen = 'true'`. Never show it in Expo Go or on emulators (capability ≠ ok → mark seen and skip). Silent path, independent of the explainer: whenever a session exists, capability is `ok`, permission is already `granted` and kv `push_token` is EMPTY (fresh install with a previously granted permission, after a sign-out, or a second account on a shared phone — `push_explainer_seen` is already set in those cases, so the modal alone would never bring the device back), call `registerForPush` silently — no modal. When a session exists and kv `push_token` is set, run `refreshPushDevice` instead (Build 3).
5. **Sign-out cleanup** `src/features/push/signOutCleanup.ts`: export `installPushSignOutCleanup(deps = defaultPushDeps())` which calls `registerBeforeSignOut(async () => { const token = await deps.kv.get('push_token'); if (token) { await deps.deleteDevice(token).catch(noop); await deps.kv.delete('push_token'); } await deps.kv.delete('push_last_seen_sync'); await Notifications.dismissAllNotificationsAsync().catch(noop); })` — the delete runs BEFORE `auth.signOut()` (RLS `user_id = auth.uid()` needs the session). A module-level side effect would run only if something imported the module, so the install is EXPLICIT: call `installPushSignOutCleanup()` exactly once from the mount effect of `useNotificationNavigation` (Build 7, mounted in `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` after the org gate), guarded by a module flag so re-mounts do not register twice. The unit test asserts `registerBeforeSignOut` was called with a function that calls `deleteDevice(token)` and clears the kv keys before `auth.signOut()` would run.
6. **Deep-link resolution (pure, tested)** `src/lib/deep-links.ts` (file name from DESIGN §11 step 10): `resolveNotificationTarget(data: unknown, ctx: { activeOrgId, orgIds })` → `{ kind: 'navigate', orgId, path } | { kind: 'ignore', reason }`: accept only `data.url` matching `^/(announcements|bulletins|events|surveys)/[0-9a-f-]{36}$` (the four shapes of `notificationTargetPath`) and `data.org_id` a uuid the user actively belongs to (`orgIds`); `events`/`surveys` → for now `ignore` with reason `not_built` (5.3 / 6.1 lift this); anything else → `ignore` (`bad_payload`, `not_member`). Never navigate on attacker-controlled arbitrary URLs.
7. **Response handling** `src/features/push/useNotificationNavigation.ts`, mounted once in `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` after the org gate (its mount effect also calls `installPushSignOutCleanup()` from Build 5 and kicks off Build 4's silent-registration / `refreshPushDevice` decision): (a) `Notifications.addNotificationResponseReceivedListener` (warm taps); (b) cold start — `Notifications.getLastNotificationResponseAsync()` (or the `useLastNotificationResponse` hook) once per app launch, deduplicated by `notification.request.identifier` stored in memory; for each → `resolveNotificationTarget(response.notification.request.content.data, …)`; on `navigate`: if `orgId !== activeOrgId` → `await switchOrg(orgId)`; then `router.push(path)` (expo-router maps `/announcements/<id>` to `app/(app)/announcements/[id].tsx`). Foreground receipt (`addNotificationReceivedListener`): invalidate the feed and bulletins queries so Home refreshes; no in-app banner beyond the system one.
8. **Notification settings** `app/(app)/settings/notifications.tsx` + `src/features/push/NotificationSettings.tsx`: section "This device" — permission status (`granted` / `denied` with "Open system settings" → `Linking.openSettings()`), registration status from kv (`Registered` / `Not registered` + "Register again" → `registerForPush`), the capability message when not `ok`; section "<org name>" — switches for **Announcements** and **Bulletins** bound to `notification_preferences` via `getNotificationPreferences(supabase, userId, orgId)` (treat a missing row as all-true defaults, matching the column defaults) and `upsertNotificationPreferences` validated by `notificationPreferencesSchema` (send all four booleans; keep `events`/`surveys` at their current/default values and do NOT show their switches until 5.3/6.1 — comment `TODO(5.3)`, `TODO(6.1)`); optimistic update with rollback + toast on error; note "Preferences are per church; switch church to change another one". Explain that turning everything off keeps the device registered (the server intersects preferences — DESIGN §8).
9. **More tab** `app/(app)/(tabs)/more.tsx` + `src/features/more/MoreMenu.tsx`: rows Bulletins → `/bulletins`, Notification settings → `/settings/notifications`, Change password → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(`${webUrl}/auth/reset`)` with helper text "Password changes happen on the web" (members created with a temporary password — DESIGN §5 path 2 — have no other way to change it), Switch church (only when `orgs.length > 1`, opens `useOrgSwitcher().open()`), Sign out (confirm dialog → `signOutEverywhere()`), a footer with "Anacast", `Application.nativeApplicationVersion`/`Constants.expoConfig?.version`, and links Privacy Policy → `${webUrl}/privacy`, Terms → `${webUrl}/terms` (`WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync`); header shows the signed-in email (`useMyContext().profile.email`) and org name. Leave `TODO(5.x)` comments where Directory, Calendar, Documents, My household, Surveys and Delete account rows will go (DESIGN §10).
10. **Tests** (Vitest, node; because `registerForPush`/`refreshPushDevice`/`installPushSignOutCleanup` take injected `PushDeps`, they are tested with plain fake objects — no `vi.mock('react-native')` needed; only `defaultPushDeps()` touches Expo modules and `src/lib/supabase.ts`, and it is not unit-tested; if any test still imports a file that reaches `react-native`, add `vi.mock('react-native', () => ({ Platform: { OS: 'android' }, AppState: { addEventListener: () => ({ remove() {} }) } }))` and `vi.mock('@/lib/supabase')`): `pushCapability` (five outcomes incl. `platform: 'web'` → `unsupported_platform`), `resolveNotificationTarget` (valid announcement, valid bulletin, event → `not_built`, foreign org → `not_member`, external URL → `bad_payload`, missing data), `registerForPush` state machine (`undetermined → granted → upsertDevice called with a schema-valid row with `platform: 'android'` and kv set`, `denied → no upsert`, `getExpoPushTokenAsync` throwing → `error`, `platform: 'web'` → `unsupported` before any permission call, stored old token ≠ new token → `deleteDevice(old)` then upsert(new)), `refreshPushDevice` (within 24 h → no calls; after 24 h with a rotated token → delete old + upsert new with `enabled: true`; same token → upsert only), and `installPushSignOutCleanup` (registers a function that deletes the device and clears `push_token`/`push_last_seen_sync`).
11. **Docs**: `apps/mobile/README.md` — a "Push" section: what is needed at build time (`google-services.json`, FCM v1 key in EAS — DESIGN §13 risk 5), why Expo Go cannot receive pushes, how to test with `npx expo start --dev-client`, and how to send a test push to a token from the Expo push tool (developer aid). `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` is 4.4's.

## Constraints
- All writes through `@church/db` helpers with the user client (RLS `user_id = auth.uid()`); never `supabase.from('push_devices')` in screens; never a service key; never call `srv_*`.
- Payload trust: only `data.url` shapes produced by `notificationTargetPath` and only orgs the user is an active member of; no `Linking.openURL(data.url)`.
- Channel id `announcements`, `projectId` from `Constants.expoConfig.extra.eas.projectId`, token via `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` — exactly as DESIGN §10; never `getDevicePushTokenAsync` for the server.
- Native dependency versions only via `npx expo install` (nothing new should be needed; `expo-application` is bundled with `expo` if you want the native version — otherwise use `Constants.expoConfig.version`).
- Do not build directory, events, surveys, join codes, account deletion (later phases). Do not touch `apps/web` (the dispatcher contract is fixed by 3.6a), migrations (never `supabase db push`), or shared packages except the additive `upsertPushDevice` `enabled: true` on-conflict change if 1.7a lacks it (with a test, recorded in HANDOFF).
- No secrets, no real tokens in tests (use `ExponentPushToken[test-token]`), no model identifiers.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green; `pnpm --filter mobile test` shows `push-capability`, `deep-links`, `registerForPush`, `refreshPushDevice`, `signOutCleanup` tests passing.
- `pnpm --filter mobile doctor` (pinned `expo-doctor`) → no issues; with the 4.1a mock env `npx expo export --platform android --output-dir dist` → succeeds (`rm -rf dist`).
- `git grep -n "'announcements'" apps/mobile/src/lib/push.ts` → the channel id; `git grep -n "getDevicePushTokenAsync\|openURL(data" apps/mobile` → nothing; `git grep -n "supabase.from(" apps/mobile/src apps/mobile/app` → nothing; `ls apps/mobile/src/lib/push` → "No such file or directory" (there is `push.ts` and `push-capability.ts`, no `push/` directory); `git grep -n "installPushSignOutCleanup()" apps/mobile/src apps/mobile/app` → exactly one call site outside tests.
- Static review: `installPushSignOutCleanup()` is actually called from a mounted component, and the device delete runs before `auth.signOut()`; `refreshPushDevice` re-fetches the Expo token and upserts `enabled: true`; `resolveNotificationTarget` rejects `https://…` in `data.url`; the explainer never appears when capability ≠ ok; `push_devices` upsert row validates against `registerPushDeviceSchema`.
- With a preview/dev build on a physical Android phone and the hosted project (step 4.5 — Checkpoint C): accept the explainer → SQL Editor `select platform, enabled, device_name from public.push_devices` shows the phone; publish an announcement on the web with push on → the notification arrives within seconds; tap it with the app killed → the announcement opens; sign out → the row is gone. Record in HANDOFF whether this was possible in this session (normally it is verified by the founder in 4.5).

## 4.5 — Expo / EAS / Firebase + Checkpoint C (founder, about 2–3 hours including build waits; a physical Android phone is required)

Follow `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` (step 4.4) for screenshots-level detail; this checklist is the ordered summary. Never paste a key, the `google-services.json` contents or a service-account JSON into git, a Claude Code prompt (`prompt_history.txt` is committed verbatim) or chat — everything goes to the password-manager vault from step 0.1.

**Before you start (must already be true)**
1. Checkpoint B is done: the web app is deployed on Vercel (`<VERCEL_URL>`), the Supabase project exists, `9999_init.sql` is pasted (HANDOFF ledger), and BOTH the Magic Link AND the Confirm signup email templates contain `{{ .Token }}` (Supabase → Authentication → Email Templates → Magic Link, then Confirm signup; 2.4 made the second optional — it is required here because an invited person without an account receives the Confirm signup email on their first code) — without them the app sends a link instead of a code and cannot sign in (DESIGN §13 risk 7).
2. You must be an **ACTIVE member** of the first church with the email you will type into the phone. As super admin your email already has an auth account (you signed up in 2.5), so use **Invite, not Create account** (Create account calls `auth.admin.createUser` and fails for an existing email; an invitation is not a membership until accepted): `/o/<slug>/users` → **Invite** → your email (no permissions needed) → if Resend is not configured, copy the link → open it in the same browser where you are signed in → **Accept**. Check that `/o/<slug>/users` now lists you as active (if the app shows the "no church" screen later, this is the item to redo). A second person with a fresh email can instead be created with Create account. The Supabase Free project must not be paused (dashboard shows "Active"; restore it if it says paused).
3. Accounts from step 0.1: Expo (expo.dev) and a Google account for Firebase. If deferred, create them now with `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` and turn on two-factor authentication.
4. On your computer: `git pull`, `pnpm install`, `cd apps/mobile`.

**A. EAS project**
5. `npx eas-cli login` → sign in with the Expo account.
6. `npx eas-cli init` → confirm creating the project under your account (slug `anacast`). Because `app.config.ts` is dynamic, EAS prints the project id instead of writing it: copy the `Project ID` (a UUID). If the command ends with an error telling you to add `extra.eas.projectId` yourself, that is expected: take the id from the message or from expo.dev → project → Overview. Record it in HANDOFF.md → "Mobile (Phase 1)" (it is not a secret) and put it in `apps/mobile/.env` as `EAS_PROJECT_ID=<id>` (the file is gitignored; eas-cli and Expo CLI read `.env` from `apps/mobile`, so `project:info` and `build` only work after this line exists).
7. Confirm with `npx eas-cli project:info` → shows `anacast` and the id.

**B. EAS environment variables (preview environment; repeat later for production)**
8. expo.dev → your project → **Environment variables** → environment **preview** → Add variable, one at a time (or use the `npx eas-cli env:create --environment preview …` commands in MOBILE_BUILD.md §4):

   - `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` = `https://<VERCEL_URL>` (the same value as Vercel's `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, no trailing slash) — plaintext.
   - `EAS_PROJECT_ID` = the id from A.6 — plaintext. If EAS refuses the name because it reserves the `EAS_` prefix, create `ANACAST_EAS_PROJECT_ID` instead and ask an agent (helper prompt below) to make `app.config.ts` read `process.env.EAS_PROJECT_ID ?? process.env.ANACAST_EAS_PROJECT_ID` — one line, recorded in HANDOFF (docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md §4 describes it).
   - `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` — type **File**, visibility **Secret** — added in C.11 after you have the file.
9. Also create the same five variables in the **development** environment if you or an agent will run development builds.

**C. Firebase project and Android app**
10. console.firebase.google.com → **Add project** → name `Anacast` → disable Google Analytics → Create. Project settings (gear) → **Your apps** → **Add app** → Android → *Android package name* = exactly the `android.package` value from `apps/mobile/app.config.ts` (print it: `npx expo config --type public | grep '"package"'` — normally `com.anacast.app`; it is immutable after the first Play upload, step 6.5) → nickname `Anacast` → Register app → **Download google-services.json** → skip the remaining SDK steps.
11. Save the downloaded file as `apps/mobile/google-services.json` (gitignored — check with `git status`, it must NOT appear) and upload it to EAS: expo.dev → Environment variables → preview → Add → name `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON`, type **File**, visibility **Secret**, choose the file → Save (or `npx eas-cli env:create --environment preview --name GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON --type file --value ./google-services.json --visibility secret`). Store a copy in the vault.
12. FCM v1 key: Firebase → Project settings → **Service accounts** → **Generate new private key** → Generate → a JSON file downloads (treat it as a password). Then `npx eas-cli credentials -p android` → select the `preview` build profile (or "All") → **Google Service Account** → **Manage your Google Service Account Key for Push Notifications (FCM V1)** → **Set up a Google Service Account Key** → Upload a new key → pick the downloaded JSON → confirm. Afterwards move the JSON into the vault and delete it from Downloads.

**D. Build and install the preview APK**
13. `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile preview` → answer **Yes** to "Generate a new Android Keystore?" (EAS stores it; you never see it) → wait (10–25 minutes on the free queue). The terminal prints a build page URL.
14. On the phone: open the build page (QR code or link) → **Install** → download the APK → if Android blocks it, allow "Install unknown apps" for your browser → install → open **Anacast**.
15. Record in HANDOFF.md "Mobile (Phase 1)" → builds ledger: `preview | <build id> | <version from app.config.ts> | <date>`.

**E. Checkpoint C — Android trial (tick every line)**
16. Sign-in: enter the email from item 2 → "Email me a code" → a 6-digit code arrives → enter it → the Home tab of your church opens. (If a link arrives instead of a code, fix the templates from item 1 and retry. If the app lands on the "no church" screen, redo item 2 — the screen tells super admins exactly that.)
17. Notifications: the explainer appears → **Turn on notifications** → Android asks for permission → Allow. Verify on the server: Supabase → SQL Editor → `select platform, enabled, device_name, created_at from public.push_devices;` → one row for your phone.
18. Push from an announcement: on the web (`/o/<slug>/announcements/new`) publish an announcement to **All attendees** with push on → the phone shows a notification within seconds → tap it → the announcement opens in the app. Then repeat with the app fully closed (swipe it away first) → the tap opens the announcement from cold start.
19. Push from a bulletin (founder decision 6, push on by default): upload a bulletin PDF on the web (`/o/<slug>/bulletins`) → notification → tap → the bulletin screen → **Open bulletin** → the phone's PDF viewer shows it.
20. Sermons: play an **uploaded mp3** → lock the phone → audio keeps playing (required); the lock screen also shows the sermon title unless HANDOFF's 4.2b "Deviations from plan" says lock-screen controls are pending the `expo-audio` API (then only continued playback counts); play a **YouTube-linked** sermon → it plays inline; open a **Google Drive-linked** sermon → the browser opens (expected, DESIGN §7). If there are no such sermons yet, create them on the web first (`/o/<slug>/sermons/new`, Upload | Link).
21. Notification settings: More → Notification settings → switch **Bulletins** off → upload another bulletin on the web → no push arrives; switch it back on.
22. Session: kill the app and reopen → still signed in. More → Sign out → SQL Editor: the `push_devices` row is gone. Sign in again (the explainer does not reappear if permission is already granted; the row comes back).
23. Optional: a second family member's phone with a second invited account — both receive the same announcement (a brand-new invited account signs in through the Confirm signup email, so this needs the Confirm signup template edit from item 1).

**F. Record**
24. HANDOFF.md → "Mobile (Phase 1)": tick the Checkpoint C items, note the EAS project id, build id, version, date, phone model + Android version, and every failure verbatim (screenshots' text, `npx eas-cli build:view` errors). Also add under "Environment status" that the EAS `preview` environment is configured. Commit and push (or hand the notes to the helper prompt below).

**Done when**: an APK built by EAS from `main` is installed on your phone; you signed in with a 6-digit code as an active member (invited and accepted on the web); `push_devices` shows your phone; an announcement and a bulletin published on the web produced notifications that opened the right screens (including from a cold start); an uploaded sermon played in the background and a YouTube-linked sermon played inline; a bulletin PDF opened; sign-out removed the device row; HANDOFF.md holds the build ledger and the Checkpoint C results.

## Goal
Help me finish Checkpoint C. I will paste below (a) my observations from the device checklist in `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` §7 / TODO 4.5 items 16–23, marked pass or fail, (b) any EAS build error (`npx eas-cli build:view <id>` output or the build page log excerpt), and (c) SQL results I ran in the Supabase SQL Editor (never keys). Triage each failure to the layer that owns it — founder configuration (EAS environment variables, Firebase, template), web dispatcher (`apps/web/src/lib/push/*`, step 3.6a/3.6b), database (`push_devices`, `notification_preferences`, `notifications`, `notification_deliveries`, `srv_audience_user_ids`), or the mobile app (4.1a–4.3) — fix what is code, tell me exactly what to click for what is configuration, and record the outcome in HANDOFF.md.

## Inputs / prior state
- Pasted observations: <PASTE: pass/fail per item, phone model, Android version, build id>
- Pasted build or runtime errors: <PASTE or "none">
- Pasted SQL results (from `select platform, enabled, device_name from public.push_devices;`, `select kind, status, attempts, last_error from public.notifications order by created_at desc limit 5;`, `select receipt_status, error from public.notification_deliveries order by created_at desc limit 5;`): <PASTE or "not run">
- If any of these are missing and you need them, ask me for the specific query or command and stop until I answer. Never ask me for a key, token, `google-services.json` or service-account contents.

## Build
1. Map each failure to the checklist in `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` §10 (troubleshooting) first. Typical mappings: a link instead of a code → the Magic Link template (existing account) or the Confirm signup template (brand-new invited account) lacks `{{ .Token }}` (founder, Supabase dashboard); "Signups not allowed for otp" → my email has no account and no pending invite (founder, web `/users` → Invite); the app shows the "no church" screen → my email has an account but no ACTIVE membership — as super admin I must Invite myself and accept the link in the browser, not Create account (founder, web `/users`); `eas env:create` refused `EAS_PROJECT_ID` → make `app.config.ts` read `process.env.EAS_PROJECT_ID ?? process.env.ANACAST_EAS_PROJECT_ID` (agent, one line, HANDOFF); build failure mentioning `google-services.json` → the file variable `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` is missing in that EAS environment; push never arrives but `push_devices` has the row → check `notifications.status`/`last_error` and `notification_deliveries.error` (`InvalidCredentials`/`MismatchSenderId` → FCM v1 key or wrong Firebase package name; `DeviceNotRegistered` → reinstall, the row is disabled; `status = 'queued'` with `attempts` growing → dispatcher/cron problem, step 3.6a/3.6b code); notification arrives but tap does nothing → `data.url`/`data.org_id` shape vs `resolveNotificationTarget` in `apps/mobile/src/lib/deep-links.ts` (write a failing test, fix); audio stops when locked → `expo-audio` plugin `enableBackgroundPlayback` or `setAudioModeAsync` in `players/Audio.tsx` (a missing lock-screen TITLE with audio still playing is not a failure if HANDOFF's 4.2b deviation list says lock-screen controls are pending); YouTube blank → the hosted page `/embed/yt/[id]` headers/CSP (3.4b) or `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` wrong in the EAS environment (rebuild needed).
2. For code fixes: smallest change in the owning package, with a regression test where a pure function exists (`playerStrategy`, `deep-links`, `capability`, `dispatch.test.ts`). Keep `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test`, `pnpm --filter mobile doctor` (pinned `expo-doctor`) and `npx expo export --platform android` green. Any fix under `apps/mobile` needs a new EAS build to reach the phone — say so explicitly and give me the command (`npx eas-cli build -p android --profile preview`).
3. For configuration fixes: give me the exact click path or `npx eas-cli …` command and what to re-run on the phone; do not guess values.
4. `HANDOFF.md` → "Mobile (Phase 1)": record the Checkpoint C results I pasted (pass/fail per item, device, build id, date), the fixes made and the configuration steps still pending; update "Environment status" (EAS preview environment configured, Firebase project exists, FCM v1 key uploaded) using only non-secret facts.
5. If everything passed: mark Checkpoint C reached in HANDOFF.md and `docs/TODO.md`, and list what M5 needs from the founder next (nothing new for 5.1; 5.7 App Links will need the signing certificate SHA-256 from `npx eas-cli credentials`).

## Constraints
- Never write a real email, key, token, project secret or file contents into the repo, the prompt history or your messages; `EAS_PROJECT_ID` and build ids are fine.
- No new features, no scope creep beyond the pasted failures; no migrations (never `supabase db push`); native dependency versions only via `npx expo install` if a fix truly needs a package (record it).
- Do not modify the 3.6a dispatcher's message contract or the 4.3 payload validation without recording the change in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" and updating both sides' tests.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` green; `pnpm --filter mobile doctor` (pinned `expo-doctor`) and the mock-env `npx expo export --platform android` succeed after any mobile change; `pnpm --filter web build` succeeds after any web change.
- Each pasted failure has either a commit that fixes it or a precise founder action in your final message; re-run instructions are explicit about whether a rebuild is required.

## Finish
- Update HANDOFF.md as in Build 4/5; tick step 4.5 in `docs/TODO.md` only if every Checkpoint C item passed or its fix is deployed and re-verified; write `session_log.md`; commit `fix(mobile): Checkpoint C triage — <one-line summary>` (or `docs: record Checkpoint C results` when nothing was fixed); push (`git push origin main` unless another branch was named). If something in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.

steps.title: Mobile post-Checkpoint-C polish round (reusable template)
steps.goal: A reusable prompt for the fix/polish round after the founder's first Android trial: the founder pastes a list of observations (UI rough edges, copy, offline behaviour, playback quirks), the agent triages, fixes, adds regression tests, rebuilds via EAS instructions and updates docs — the mobile counterpart of step 3.10.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 4.6 "Mobile post-Checkpoint-C polish round (reusable template)" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` (§7 device checklist, §10 troubleshooting), `docs/MEDIA.md`, `HANDOFF.md` ("Mobile (Phase 1)": builds ledger, known gaps, Deviations from plan) and `docs/PLAN.md` §9–§10 (mobile screen map, cut list) before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
Checkpoint C (step 4.5) is reached or nearly reached: the preview APK from EAS runs on my phone and I have used it for a while. Below I paste a numbered list of observations from that use — rough edges in the UI, wrong or unclear copy, offline behaviour, playback quirks, notification timing, anything that annoyed me. When you finish, every observation has been classified and dealt with: bugs and copy problems are fixed in the owning file with a regression test wherever a pure function exists, configuration problems come back to me as an exact click path or `npx eas-cli …` command, limitations are documented, and out-of-scope ideas are filed for a later phase. You tell me precisely which fixes need a new EAS build to reach the phone and give me the command. This is the mobile counterpart of step 3.10 (web fix/polish round) and, like it, is a reusable template: I may paste a new list into a fresh session more than once.

## Inputs / prior state
- My observations: <PASTE a numbered list — one observation per line, with the phone model, Android version and the build id from HANDOFF's builds ledger; say "pass" for checklist items that worked so you do not re-verify them>.
- Optional pasted material: `npx eas-cli build:view <id>` output, text of an error toast, or SQL results I ran in the Supabase SQL Editor (never keys). If you need a specific query or command from me, ask for exactly that one and stop until I answer. Never ask me for a key, token, `google-services.json` or service-account contents.
- The app as built in 4.1a–4.3 (package `mobile`), by area: auth `apps/mobile/src/features/auth/*` (`SessionProvider`, `SignInForm`, `OtpForm`, `useAcceptInvitation`, `otpOptions`, `authErrors`, `signOut.ts` with `registerBeforeSignOut`) and `src/features/org/*` (`ActiveOrgProvider`, `resolveActiveOrg`, `OrgSwitcher`); feed `src/features/feed/*` (`useFeed`, `sortFeed`, `AnnouncementCard`, `BulletinCard`, `AnnouncementDetail`, `LinkifiedText`); bulletins `src/features/bulletins/*` (`BulletinList`, `BulletinDetail`, `OpenPdf.ts` with `openBulletinFile`/`pickOpener`); sermons `src/features/sermons/*` (`SermonList`, `SermonDetail`, `playerStrategy.ts` → `resolvePlayer`, `SermonPlayer.tsx`, `SignedMedia.tsx`, `players/{Audio,Video,YouTubeWebView,External}.tsx`); push `src/features/push/*` (`usePushOnboarding`, `useNotificationNavigation`, `NotificationSettings`, `signOutCleanup.ts`) and `src/lib/push.ts` (`registerForPush`, `refreshPushDevice`, `defaultPushDeps`), `src/lib/push-capability.ts`, `src/lib/deep-links.ts` (`resolveNotificationTarget`); shared `src/lib/{supabase,query-client,kv,env,signed-url,links}.ts`, `src/theme/tokens.ts` + `src/theme.ts`, `src/components/{Screen,LoadingState,ErrorState,EmptyState}.tsx`; routes under `apps/mobile/app/`.
- Contracts owned elsewhere — read before touching anything that crosses them: the push message shape from the web dispatcher `apps/web/src/lib/push/dispatch.ts` (3.6a: `data: { url: notificationTargetPath(kind, refId), org_id, kind, ref_id, notification_id }`, `channelId: 'announcements'`); the hosted YouTube page `apps/web/app/(public)/embed/yt/[id]/page.tsx` or `app/(share)/embed/yt/[id]/page.tsx` (3.4b); `parseMediaLink` and `youtubeHostedEmbedUrl` in `packages/domain` (1.6a/1.6b, table-tested; the web `SermonPlayer` uses the same parser); the `@church/db` queries and `queryKeys` (1.7a); `shouldPersistQuery` (1.7a) used by the persister.
- Founder decisions that bound this round: 5 (downloads exist on the share page only — the app streams, no offline downloads), 6 (bulletin pushes are on by default; a per-church toggle exists on the web and per-user switches in the app), 9 / orchestrator decision 5 (Anacast, `com.anacast.app` unless HANDOFF records another confirmed value — immutable after the first Play upload; scheme `anacast`), 10 (Supabase Free: a paused project shows up as "Network request failed" — configuration, not code). The PLAN §10 cut list says what may be dropped if time runs out and what must never be cut (push registration, sign-in, playback of uploads).
- Known gaps already recorded in HANDOFF "Mobile (Phase 1)" (e.g. lock-screen controls pending the `expo-audio` API, iOS untested, App Links in 5.7, join codes in 5.6, directory in 5.2) are not bugs — if I report one, answer with the pointer, do not build it.

## Build
1. **Classify first, then act.** Copy my list into `Session log/<this session>/triage.md` and give every item a class: `bug` (behaviour differs from the TODO step's Done-when or from PLAN §9), `copy` (wording, punctuation, capitalisation, unclear message), `ux` (layout, spacing, touch target, loading/empty/error state, ordering), `config` (EAS environment, Firebase, Supabase template/SMTP, paused project, wrong `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` in the build), `limitation` (documented gap or platform behaviour we accept), `later` (Phase 2+ feature or PLAN §10 cut-list item). Write the class and the owning file(s) next to each item before changing anything; ask me only when an item is ambiguous between `bug` and `later`.
2. **One commit per observation group.** Group related items (e.g. three copy fixes on the sign-in screen) and make one commit per group with a message that lists the item numbers (`fix(mobile): sign-in copy (#3, #7)`). Never mix a behaviour fix with unrelated copy changes in one commit, so a bad fix can be reverted alone.
3. **Regression test first for pure functions.** For `bug` items in `resolvePlayer`, `resolveNotificationTarget`, `pushCapability`, `registerForPush`/`refreshPushDevice` (injected `PushDeps`), `resolveActiveOrg`, `sortFeed`, `bulletinRangeLabel`, `pickOpener`, `isSignedUrlExpired`, `parseAppLink`, `otpOptions`, `authErrors`: add the failing case to the existing Vitest table, watch it fail, then fix. Component-level bugs (layout, state) get a fix plus a static-review note in the commit body, since the mobile package has no jsdom/RN test renderer.
4. **Shared-package changes are rare and symmetrical.** If a fix truly belongs in `packages/domain` (a link shape `parseMediaLink` misparses) or `packages/db` (a query filter), change it there with a test AND run the web tests — the web `SermonPlayer` and share page use the same parser; never change the parser's strategy names, `youtubeHostedEmbedUrl`, `notificationTargetPath` shapes or `queryKeys` without updating both consumers' tests in the same commit and recording it in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan". Never touch `apps/web` otherwise.
5. **Copy and UX rules.** Keep the neutral theme: colours only in `src/theme/tokens.ts`. Copy stays plain, never blames the user, and names the actor ("Ask your church to…", "Open the web app to…"). Every message that comes from an error keeps using `DomainError`/`authErrors` mapping — no raw error text on screen. Respect the system font scale and keep `accessibilityLabel`s when you restructure a screen.
6. **Config items.** For each `config` item write the exact fix for me: dashboard click path or `npx eas-cli …` command, which EAS environment (`preview`/`production`), and whether a rebuild is needed (any `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` change or `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` change → rebuild; a Supabase template or SMTP change → no rebuild). Add the symptom → cause → fix line to `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` §10 if it is not there.
7. **Limitations and later items.** `limitation` → one sentence in `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` §10 or `docs/MEDIA.md` (whichever the user would look at) and a line under HANDOFF "Mobile (Phase 1) known gaps"; `later` → a line under the relevant TODO step (5.x/6.x) in `docs/TODO.md` notes or HANDOFF "Phase 4 ideas", with my item number so I can find it.
8. **Rebuild list.** Keep a running list of which commits change anything under `apps/mobile` (they need `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile preview` to reach the phone) versus web/docs-only commits (live after the Vercel deploy). Put the list in your final message and in `session_log.md`.
9. **Do not** add features, redesign screens, upgrade Expo or any dependency, or start Phase 2 work in this round. A dependency bump is a `later` item unless a pasted crash proves it is required — then `npx expo install` it and record the pin in HANDOFF.

## Constraints
- Native dependency versions only via `npx expo install` (record any addition in HANDOFF "Version pins"); never `expo-av`, never `react-native-youtube-iframe`, never a `youtube.com/embed` `source.uri`.
- No elevated Supabase key, no `srv_*` calls, no `supabase.from(` in screens; all reads/writes through `@church/db` helpers with the user client; schemas only from `@church/domain`.
- Migrations are out of scope (never `supabase db push`); if an observation needs a schema change, file it as `later` with the proposed `9998_*` file name and stop.
- Never write a real email, key, token, build log with secrets, or my phone's identifiers beyond model + Android version into the repo or `prompt_history.txt`.
- Do not modify the 3.6a dispatcher contract or the 4.3 payload validation unless a test on both sides proves the bug; record such a change under "Deviations from plan".

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green; `pnpm --filter mobile test` shows every new regression case passing (list them in the commit body).
- `pnpm --filter mobile doctor` (pinned `expo-doctor`) → no issues; with the mock env (`EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://localhost:54321 EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_ci_placeholder EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL=http://localhost:3000`) `npx expo export --platform android --output-dir dist` → succeeds (`rm -rf dist`). `pnpm --filter web build` after any change under `apps/web` or `packages/*`.
- The guard greps from 4.1b–4.3 still return nothing: `git grep -n "z.object" apps/mobile/src`; `git grep -n "anacast://" apps/mobile/src apps/mobile/app -- ':!*.test.ts'`; `git grep -n "supabase.from(" apps/mobile/src apps/mobile/app`; `git grep -n "SUPABASE_SECRET\|service_role\|auth.admin" apps/mobile`; `git grep -n "expo-av\|react-native-youtube-iframe" apps/mobile`; `git grep -n "/embed/yt" apps/mobile/src` → tests only; `git grep -n "3600\|50 \* 60" apps/mobile/src` → nothing; `git grep -n "getDevicePushTokenAsync\|openURL(data" apps/mobile` → nothing.
- `Session log/<this session>/triage.md` has a class and an owning file for every pasted item, and every `bug` item points at a commit hash.
- If a development build is on my phone, I re-test the fixed items myself after the rebuild; tell me which items to re-test.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: "Mobile (Phase 1)" — update the known-gaps list (add limitations, remove anything you fixed), append a row to the builds ledger placeholder for the rebuild I must run (`preview | <pending> | <version> | <date>` — I fill in the build id), and add the Checkpoint C follow-up status; "Deviations from plan" — any shared-package or contract change; "Phase 4 ideas" / the relevant 5.x/6.x TODO notes — the `later` items with my item numbers; "Version pins" — any `expo install`.
- `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` §10 and `docs/MEDIA.md` — the symptom → cause → fix lines and limitations from Build 6–7.
